purpose: Held-out interventions that require extrapolation. The study's four held-out contrasts (feed-concentration increase and decrease, jacket warming and cooling) used steps of the same kinds and sizes as training, with responses of 7 to 11 K inside the 5 to 18 K range the training runs cover, so a fit around the one operating point interpolates them. These are the same four contrasts with steps twice and three times the largest training step, held long enough for the temperature to settle at a level training never reached. Designed on 2026-11-11 at the user's request from public information only (the public prompt, the public training trajectories and the protocol's input encoding), and frozen before any reference response was computed and before any model was scored on them. Every scored model was frozen beforehand.

design_basis.input_units: Specification values scale the training steps: Cf 0.25 and Tjf 12 K per unit, read from the public training trajectories.
design_basis.training_range: Training inputs moved Cf within 0.75-1.25 and Tjf within 318-342 K (largest steps of one unit in each direction), and the temperature within 349.9-377.0 K, responses of 5 to 18 K.
design_basis.timing: Each step starts at t = 10 and ends at t = 20 of the 30-unit horizon: the temperature settles within a few time units (public training data), so the response reaches its new level and the return after the step ends is observed too.
design_basis.preparation: No probe shifts an initial value; the hidden quantities start from their fixed preparation (public prompt, section B).

probes.name: jacket_warming_2x
probes.rationale: Tjf to 354 K; training reached 342 K.

probes.name: jacket_cooling_2x
probes.rationale: Tjf to 306 K; training reached 318 K.

probes.name: jacket_warming_3x
probes.rationale: Tjf to 366 K, above the reactor's operating temperature.

metrics: The study's own (scripts/iclr_anchor_fidelity.py evaluate_one): response RSE against the matched basal control, direction and peak time of the T response, windowed direction, and absolute NMSE. A model whose rollout fails counts as failed.
